Q: Why is the reference returned from ImmutableArray<T>.Builder.ItemRef(Int32) readonly? A:

Ah - it's probably because, if MoveToImmutable() is called, the builder's backing array is used as the backing array for the resulting ImmutableArray<T>, so the reference would become a reference into an ImmutableArray<T>.

The other API method which lets you mutate an ImmutableArray<T> is quite obscure, but this would be more visible and thus more likely to be accidentally misused.

Q: Unity Project doesn't have solution file A:

For me the solution was to make sure that all packages that the project depends on are in manifest.json inside Packages folder and also actually installed and imported. Then after that, I pressed Asset - Reimport All inside Unity Editor. During Reimport All it created solution and project files as well as resolved all dependencies and the project was successfully built and started.

Q: installutil bindingRedirect A:

This answer is far from ideal, but it does work... It's just spelling out what Tom Glider's answer is alluding to...

As per the question - The problem is when InstallUtil.exe attempts to install your windows service - but is unable to create an instance of your serviceInstaller class (via reflection) due to binding redirects it can't load. You'll probably get an error logged similar to:

Installing assembly 'C:\PathToExe\MainService.exe'.
Affected parameters are:
   logtoconsole = 
   assemblypath = C:\PathToExe\MainService.exe
   logfile = C:\PathToExe\MainServer.InstallLog
Unable to create an instance of the YourNamespace.MainServiceInstaller installer type.
System.Reflection.TargetInvocationException: Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation.
The inner exception System.IO.FileNotFoundException was thrown with the following error message: Could not load file or assembly 'Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Abstractions, Version=3.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=adb9793829ddae60' or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified..

In this case the workaround is to

  1. Go to C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v4.0.30319

  2. Copy InstallUtil.exe, InstallUtil.exe.config and InstallUtilLib.dll and put them somewhere else

  3. Open your the .exe.config file of the assembly containing your service installer

  4. Copy the entire <runtime> section (which has the binding redirects) and place into InstallUtil.exe.config

  5. Run the copy of your InstallUtil.exe to install your service. - ie
    InstallUtil.exe <path_to_serviceExe>

  6. To uninstall run the copy of InstallUtil.exe with the \u parameter:
    InstallUtil.exe \u <path_to_serviceExe>

Q: uncommon "setting an array with a sequence" error A:

Your metric needs to take in two vectors, and output a scalar. It currently outputs a tuple.

For example, this would work:

def dum_cusmet(x, x2):
  return np.sum(np.abs(x - x2))

However, what you're doing now fails on this line

  File ".../sklearn/metrics/pairwise.py", line 2045, in _pairwise_callable
    out[i, j] = metric(x, y, **kwds)

because metric is returning two vectors, and out[i, j] = ... is expecting a scalar.
